title: [Atlas][P1] Unrelated upserts discard the negation abstention ledger
body:
## Scope and evidence
Audited commit: `b0c33d2f6567a2c741240f3c44bc00ca2f01e7e7` on `maestro/rebuild-fork-dev-clean` (not default `dev`). Follow-up to ATL-001 in draft PR #14.

**Confirmed by original source inspection; runtime reproduction results will be attached separately, not assumed.**

## Observed defect
`StoreProjection` carries optional `abstained`, a map of durable `AbstainedRecord` values keyed by negation identity. Its documented lifecycle is to retain an abstention until the corresponding negation is admitted. However `upsert()` copies only `current` and `cas`, then returns `store: { current, cas }` for every route, including DEDUP. It does not preserve `store.abstained` (or projection-level `builtAt`).

Source: https://github.com/gmhelmold/HuGR-Orchestra/blob/b0c33d2f6567a2c741240f3c44bc00ca2f01e7e7/foundation/atlas/packages/knowledge/src/write/upsert.ts

A normal governed emit publishes the returned projection. Thus an unrelated fact write can remove the abstention ledger instead of merely adding/updating that fact. An unrelated upsert is not an authorized supersession of those records.

## Minimal regression
Start with a projection containing an abstention at key A. Apply an unrelated CREATE at key B. Assert A survives with identical reason/witness and the input is not mutated. Repeat for UPDATE, SUPERSEDE and DEDUP. Exercise the real disk-backed governed emit and reopen the store to prove retention across serialization and reload.

## Impact and limits
Loss of evidence explaining why negative facts could not be established. This is not proof of a false negative, unauthorized mutation or loss of every state field. P1 is proposed for silent loss of an explicitly durable ledger.

## Completeness criteria
Cover all upsert routes and callers publishing their projections; distinguish preservation of unrelated metadata from legitimate matching-key mutation at the negation door.

## Success criteria
Unrelated writes and duplicates preserve existing abstentions through reopen. Admitting a negation removes only its matching abstention.

## Quality standards
Import original reducer/door; use real disk persistence in the integration test. Do not duplicate product logic or replace persistence with a success-only mock. Include controls.

## Definition of done
Regression fails on this commit and passes with the fix; existing negation/upsert suites pass; record commands, versions, commit and outputs. No closure based only on typecheck.

## Invariants
Preserve unrelated projection fields by default; no unauthorized ledger deletion; no mutation of reducer inputs; no weakening of authz/ratification; preserve legitimate same-key supersession.

title: [Atlas][P1] Facts dropped from query output earn delivery hits and become governing
body:
## Scope and evidence
Commit `b0c33d2f6567a2c741240f3c44bc00ca2f01e7e7`, branch `maestro/rebuild-fork-dev-clean`; follow-up to ATL-002 / draft audit PR #14.

**Reproduced with original compiled Atlas, original BLAKE3 kernel, real temporary Git repository and disk store, real `composeRuntime` and its public `handler.handle` path.** Node v22.17.1, macOS. No query/ledger/grounding/persistence doubles and no LLM calls. This is handler integration, not a live MCP transport test.

## Actual reproduction
Create six source files and emit six T2 facts with different anchors, each with a 450-character claim, using runtime draft and governed emit. Reuse the same runtime for nine `atlas-query` requests over `src`.

Queries 1–8 each return four advisory facts and `advisoryDropped: 2`. The same two facts never appear in either returned band. Query 9 returns **all six as T1/governing**, including those two never-delivered facts. Reopening the disk projection confirms all six stored tiers remain T2: the defect is in the served classification, not a permanent tier mutation.

## Cause
`createProjectionQueryIndex.cover()` calls `hits.logHit()` for every eligible advisory candidate before `createQuery()` calls `splitBands()`. The latter discards candidates outside the advisory budget. The USE_THRESHOLD=8 counter therefore measures pre-selection exposure, while its contract calls it served/delivered use. On the next query `servedClass()` raises the item into the uncapped governing band.

Immutable sources:
- https://github.com/gmhelmold/HuGR-Orchestra/blob/b0c33d2f6567a2c741240f3c44bc00ca2f01e7e7/foundation/atlas/packages/adapter-io/src/projection-query-index.ts
- https://github.com/gmhelmold/HuGR-Orchestra/blob/b0c33d2f6567a2c741240f3c44bc00ca2f01e7e7/foundation/atlas/packages/tools/src/query.ts
- https://github.com/gmhelmold/HuGR-Orchestra/blob/b0c33d2f6567a2c741240f3c44bc00ca2f01e7e7/foundation/atlas/packages/knowledge/src/lifecycle/hits.ts

Existing `projection-query-index.use-or-seal.test.ts` stops at `cover()` and never exercises final band selection; it does not contradict this reproduction.

## Proposed correction
Record delivered IDs only after final output membership is known. Preserve the rule that this delivery's hit affects the next classification, not the current one. Track selection attempts separately if useful.

## Completeness criteria
Trace every production query mode and final formatter; handle dropped candidates, actual delivery, repeated reads, failures, and human-sealed nodes.

## Success criteria
A never-returned fact receives zero delivery hits and cannot rise by use; returned facts increment once; legitimate threshold crossing affects the next pack; stored tiers remain unchanged unless a separately authorized operation changes them.

## Quality standards
Regression traverses the real handler and final pack, not just `cover`; fixtures use admissible-sized individual facts and real persistence. Assert exact returned IDs and original tier controls.

## Definition of done
Reproducer fails the intended delivery invariant before the fix, passes after, and the existing use-or-seal, band and query suites pass. Record exact commands and outputs.

## Invariants
Delivery is not candidate selection; dropped facts cannot acquire governing authority via fabricated use; no regression of scope, freshness, provenance or legitimate sealing.

title: [Atlas][P1] Long-lived runtime certifies stale grounding with the new HEAD watermark
body:
## Scope and evidence
Audited SHA: `b0c33d2f6567a2c741240f3c44bc00ca2f01e7e7`, `maestro/rebuild-fork-dev-clean`. Newly reproduced during the follow-up to draft audit PR #14.

**Original runtime integration:** real `initAst`, `composeRuntime`, draft/check/handler, Git commits, disk store and BLAKE3 kernel. No substituted truth gate, storage, query or hash implementation. Node v22.17.1 on macOS. This reproduction exercises the handler used by transports, not a live MCP connection.

## Reproduction and observed behavior
1. Commit C1 contains `export const value0 = 0;`.
2. Construct runtime R and draft a fact anchored to `src/f0.ts`; its revision is C1.
3. Change the source to `export const value0 = 987;` and commit C2 while R remains alive.
4. Submit the old fact through R's `atlas-emit`, explicitly using C2 as `at`.
5. **Write succeeds.** Query through R returns the fact with `freshness: FRESH` and pack `stale: false`.
6. Construct R2 against the unchanged C2 repository. R2's query returns that fact as `STALE`; R2's check rejects the identical fact at the truth gate (`wouldEmit: false`, ungrounded).

Thus two runtimes over the same current repository disagree on freshness, and the old one falsely reports a newly committed stale citation as current. The fresh query still has pack-level `stale: false`: the new-HEAD watermark obscures the mismatch even though its per-fact oracle detects it.

## Cause
`composeRuntime` builds axes once. `buildGate(axes)` explicitly ignores `at` and re-derives against those captured axes. Persistence separately resolves live HEAD and `stampGeneration` assigns that revision to newly written content. The producer therefore verified C1 but labels its output as derived at C2.

This differs from the already-addressed carry-forward watermark issue: the problem here is **new content produced by an old runtime**, not an unrelated write restamping an unchanged old row.

Sources:
- https://github.com/gmhelmold/HuGR-Orchestra/blob/b0c33d2f6567a2c741240f3c44bc00ca2f01e7e7/foundation/atlas/packages/adapter-io/src/compose.ts
- https://github.com/gmhelmold/HuGR-Orchestra/blob/b0c33d2f6567a2c741240f3c44bc00ca2f01e7e7/foundation/atlas/packages/adapter-io/src/grounding-computer.ts
- https://github.com/gmhelmold/HuGR-Orchestra/blob/b0c33d2f6567a2c741240f3c44bc00ca2f01e7e7/foundation/atlas/packages/adapter-io/src/freshness-watermark.ts

## Proposed correction
Bind each verification and publication to the same explicit source snapshot. When current repository state differs, refresh/rebuild safely or refuse pending refresh; never stamp a revision the oracle did not verify. Consider both committed changes and dirty worktree changes explicitly. A HEAD comparison alone does not settle dirty-tree correctness.

## Completeness criteria
Audit runtime lifetime, captured axes, write `at`, row stamps and read flags; include new facts, updates, duplicates, unrelated commits, changed sources, dirty worktrees and a revision change during publication.

## Success criteria
Old grounding cannot be newly admitted and certified current after its source changes. Rebuilt and retained runtimes agree or the retained runtime reports an explicit stale/refresh refusal. Unchanged-source controls continue working under the defined snapshot policy.

## Quality standards
Real commits and original composition; assert admission result, per-fact freshness and persisted revision independently. No constant freshness mocks and no collapsing the two freshness notions to hide disagreement.

## Definition of done
A regression demonstrates the current false-FRESH result, passes after correction, and relevant query/grounding/watermark/MCP-lifetime tests pass. Preserve the new-runtime refusal control.

## Invariants
Verified revision equals certified revision; `FRESH` never derives from an obsolete index while claiming current state; durability and authz remain intact; unknown/currentness failures are explicit.

title: [Atlas][P2] Draft advertises full ratification but drops the provenance that would require it
body:
## Scope / evidence
SHA `b0c33d2f6567a2c741240f3c44bc00ca2f01e7e7`, feature branch `maestro/rebuild-fork-dev-clean`. Original built Atlas, real `initAst`/`composeRuntime`, Git fixture, policy, BLAKE3 and disk persistence; no planner, gate or store doubles. No ratification token in the test process. Related audit PR #14.

## Reproduced behavior
On an authorized fixture scope, call `runtime.draft({anchor:'src/f0.ts',slot:'invariant',claim:'Fixture value0 is exported.'})`.

Actual draft reports `route:'full-ratify'`, `requires:'ATLAS_RATIFY_TOKEN'`, but `draft.fact.provenance` is absent. Without modifying that fact, `runtime.check(draft.fact,draft.rev)` reports `wouldEmit:true` with all gates passing, and public `handler.handle('atlas-emit', {node:draft.fact,at:draft.rev})` persists it successfully without a ratifier.

## Root cause
The draft planner's `candidateView` includes `DRAFT_PROVENANCE={source:'atlas-draft',trusted:false}` when it calculates `route`. Its separately constructed output fact omits that provenance. The real emit gate consequently sees a different candidate: absent provenance is legacy-compatible in the fast path. A decision about one payload is advertised for another.

Sources:
- https://github.com/gmhelmold/HuGR-Orchestra/blob/b0c33d2f6567a2c741240f3c44bc00ca2f01e7e7/foundation/atlas/packages/tools/src/draft.ts
- https://github.com/gmhelmold/HuGR-Orchestra/blob/b0c33d2f6567a2c741240f3c44bc00ca2f01e7e7/foundation/atlas/packages/knowledge/src/ratify/fastpath.ts

## Impact and qualification
Planner guidance and enforced policy disagree; origin/trust information used to justify the guidance is lost. This is not a demonstrated remote-authentication bypass or a claim that every authored T2 advisory must require human ratification. Decide the intended draft-origin policy explicitly and make the returned fact and route describe the same policy.

## Completeness criteria
Cover draft and draftSupersede, new and occupied identities, absent/false/true provenance, unratified and ratified calls, and all channels consuming the returned fact.

## Success criteria
For unchanged source/store/policy, the planner's ratification route agrees with check and emit on the exact returned fact. Trust information is preserved or explicitly and consistently classified; the no-token control cannot contradict the reported requirement.

## Quality standards
Run original composition with no input edits between draft, check and emit; verify actual persisted CAS bytes and controls. Do not replace an expected denial with a fake gate.

## Definition of done
Regression demonstrates the mismatch before the fix and agreement after; existing authoring and governance tests pass, and intended compatibility for legacy absent provenance is documented.

## Invariants
The routed candidate and emitted candidate share the same trust semantics; no silent loss of provenance; no weakening of existing predicate/T0/promoted ratification or actor scope checks.

title: [Own][P1] Gotchas retain stored FRESH after their grounded source changes
body:
## Scope and proof
SHA `b0c33d2f6567a2c741240f3c44bc00ca2f01e7e7`, `maestro/rebuild-fork-dev-clean`; strengthens OWN-003 in audit PR #14.

**Reproduced using original compiled product and kernel, real Git commits, real disk persistence, real source-derived grounding and `composeRuntime().own`.** No replacement freshness oracle. A NEW runtime is built after source mutation, so this is independent of #18's long-lived-index defect.

## Actual experiment
At C1, draft and ratify two T1 facts anchored to the same source file, one in `invariant`, one in `gotcha`. Both initially return FRESH. Change that source file and commit C2; construct a fresh runtime over C2 and read Own.

Observed:
- Own invariant freshness: `DRIFTED`.
- Own gotcha freshness: **`FRESH`**.
- Query through the same fresh runtime marks both claims `STALE` in its per-fact presentation.

`STALE` and `DRIFTED` are distinct surface representations and are not silently equated here. The problem is the gotcha's unchanged FRESH, not the vocabulary difference between query and Own.

## Cause
`buildOwnSources` passes its live freshness oracle to governing invariants and advisory bands but not to `governingGotchas`. The latter returns the original stored `GroundedFact`, including write-time freshness. `createOwn` puts that full object into the returned pack. The comment claiming this freshness has no reader is contradicted by the returned payload and static materializer's freshness check.

Sources:
- https://github.com/gmhelmold/HuGR-Orchestra/blob/b0c33d2f6567a2c741240f3c44bc00ca2f01e7e7/foundation/atlas/packages/adapter-io/src/own-bands.ts
- https://github.com/gmhelmold/HuGR-Orchestra/blob/b0c33d2f6567a2c741240f3c44bc00ca2f01e7e7/foundation/atlas/packages/adapter-io/src/own-source.ts
- https://github.com/gmhelmold/HuGR-Orchestra/blob/b0c33d2f6567a2c741240f3c44bc00ca2f01e7e7/foundation/atlas/packages/retrieval/src/own.ts

## Completeness criteria
Cover gotcha and rationale slots, fresh/changed/deleted/malformed anchors, all governing tiers, read projection and static export consumers; preserve original CAS bytes during reads.

## Success criteria
Every returned gotcha carries the current oracle verdict for its own grounding, or is explicitly held/excluded under the declared policy. No stale gotcha passes a fresh-only consumer because of a retained write-time flag.

## Quality standards
Keep paired invariant/gotcha controls over the SAME source and a newly composed runtime. Assert before/after/reopen; do not use a constant stale oracle as the only regression.

## Definition of done
The observed false-FRESH reproducer fails the intended invariant before the fix and passes after; original Own/band/static-materialization suites pass and comments accurately describe served fields.

## Invariants
Stored freshness is not current freshness; all served bands use the same source snapshot; read projection does not mutate CAS; no conflation of structural freshness with semantic truth.

title: [Own][P2] Snapshot verifier and materializer accept dangling drill targets
body:
## Scope and evidence
Audited SHA `b0c33d2f6567a2c741240f3c44bc00ca2f01e7e7`, branch `maestro/rebuild-fork-dev-clean`; OWN-001 in audit PR #14.

Reproduced through the ORIGINAL `parseOwnSnapshot`, `exportOwnSnapshot`, materializer and verifier, then the ORIGINAL `scripts/materialize-own-snapshot.mjs` and `harness/gates/own-snapshot-guard.mjs`. Real BLAKE3 implementation, temporary Git repository, valid ancestor commit and actual matching source blob; no replacement hash implementation.

## Reproduction
Take a valid one-unit snapshot for canonical unit `src` and add `pack.drill.finer = [{level:'module',id:'missing/unit',grounding:null}]`. Do NOT add that target to `snapshot.units` and do not create its skill artifact.

Observed: parser/export accept; pure verification returns READY; materializer exits 0 and writes the snapshot/skills; guard exits 0. The emitted skill instructs the consumer to load the canonical own_* name for the missing unit, although no corresponding artifact exists.

Controls: unmodified valid snapshot passes; modifying the real source file after materialization makes the guard exit 1. The active guard is not being bypassed.

## Cause
The snapshot parser validates each `drill.finer` entry's local shape but does not validate cross-unit referential integrity. Materialization and byte comparison faithfully reproduce the dangling pointer, so exact output equality cannot detect the invalid relationship.

Sources:
- https://github.com/gmhelmold/HuGR-Orchestra/blob/b0c33d2f6567a2c741240f3c44bc00ca2f01e7e7/foundation/atlas/packages/retrieval/src/own-snapshot.ts
- https://github.com/gmhelmold/HuGR-Orchestra/blob/b0c33d2f6567a2c741240f3c44bc00ca2f01e7e7/foundation/atlas/packages/retrieval/src/own-artifact.ts
- https://github.com/gmhelmold/HuGR-Orchestra/blob/b0c33d2f6567a2c741240f3c44bc00ca2f01e7e7/specs/hugr-maestro/own-protocol.md

## Impact / limits
A supposedly validated ownership navigation path can end in a nonexistent skill and force HOLD. This does not prove current committed Genesis artifacts already contain such a pointer; it proves the proposed protocol's target-existence invariant is not enforced for accepted input.

## Completeness criteria
Validate references against the canonical snapshot unit universe and its expected artifact set; cover missing targets, removed units, duplicate units, valid shared targets and multi-level traversal. Define cyclic-pointer policy explicitly rather than inventing a blanket prohibition.

## Success criteria
Dangling target input is refused before installation and independently rejected by verification. A complete valid target set passes unchanged.

## Quality standards
Test real compiled contracts and real Git scripts, including actual output existence. Keep ancestor/blob controls; do not replace kernel identity or infer targets from prose.

## Definition of done
Current accepting reproduction becomes an explicit HOLD/nonzero rejection, valid controls pass, and Own parser/materializer/guard suites pass.

## Invariants
Every emitted drill target names an existing canonical unit and artifact; byte reproducibility is not referential validity; no partial installation on refusal; no guessed fallback retrieval.

title: [Own][P2] Malformed predicate checks render undefined and pass the static snapshot gate
body:
## Scope / evidence
SHA `b0c33d2f6567a2c741240f3c44bc00ca2f01e7e7`, feature branch `maestro/rebuild-fork-dev-clean`; OWN-002 in audit PR #14.

Reproduced with original compiled parser/exporter/materializer/verifier, original BLAKE3 kernel and ORIGINAL materialization/guard scripts against a real Git fixture with matching immutable revision/blob anchors. No replacement implementation.

## Actual input and result
Add this gotcha to an otherwise valid reviewed snapshot:
```json
{"id":"bad-check","kind":"predicate","tier":"T1","freshness":"FRESH","check":{"expr":"valid expression without required discriminant"}}
```
The missing `check.kind` is the defect-bearing field. Parser/export accept it, the generated governing fact line ends in `: undefined`, the pure verifier returns READY, materialization writes the artifacts with exit 0 and the guard also exits 0.

Controls: normal snapshot materializes and verifies; a real source edit after materialization is rejected with exit 1. Output existence was checked; a no-op script invocation was not counted as acceptance.

## Cause
`isFact()` in own-snapshot.ts accepts any predicate whose check has either a string expr OR query, without enforcing the discriminated union. `claimOf()` in own-artifact.ts reads expr only for `check.kind === 'assertion'`, and query otherwise. A shape accepted by the parser is therefore not safe for the renderer. Recomposition reproduces the same corruption, so byte equality is insufficient.

Sources:
- https://github.com/gmhelmold/HuGR-Orchestra/blob/b0c33d2f6567a2c741240f3c44bc00ca2f01e7e7/foundation/atlas/packages/retrieval/src/own-snapshot.ts
- https://github.com/gmhelmold/HuGR-Orchestra/blob/b0c33d2f6567a2c741240f3c44bc00ca2f01e7e7/foundation/atlas/packages/retrieval/src/own-artifact.ts

## Impact / limit
Invalid knowledge input can be certified as a structurally valid static ownership artifact while losing its check text. This is not a claim that the committed Genesis snapshot currently contains this malformed predicate, or that structural validation proves semantic truth.

## Completeness criteria
Validate each supported check kind with its required matching fields; cover missing/unknown kinds, expr/query mismatches, malformed nested values and valid variants. Audit parser/renderer agreement for other accepted fact families without inventing unsupported semantics.

## Success criteria
Every accepted predicate has a well-defined rendered claim; malformed input is refused before installation and independently by verification; no generated fact line contains undefined due to missing fields.

## Quality standards
Original kernel and scripts, real Git anchors, active valid/stale controls. Prefer one authoritative runtime shape contract shared with render consumption rather than two drifting approximations.

## Definition of done
Current accepting reproducer becomes an explicit rejection, valid predicate variants pass, and parser/materializer/guard regressions pass.

## Invariants
Parsing guarantees the fields rendering consumes; no corruption is legitimized by deterministic recomposition; no partial output replacement on invalid input; semantic truth and shape validity remain distinct.

title: [Maestro][P2] Re-presenting the same revision reuses an old message binding and cannot accept the new reply
body:
## Scope / evidence level
SHA `b0c33d2f6567a2c741240f3c44bc00ca2f01e7e7`, `maestro/rebuild-fork-dev-clean`; strengthens MAE-001 in audit PR #14.

**Original internal integration reproduced:** `presentApprovalFromSession` → real Effect services / SQLite event persistence and projectors → original rendered presentation → `recordApproval`. No replacement approval evaluator or producer. Visible tool-output parts were inserted as fixtures because the public `maestro_present_approval` tool is intentionally disabled pending durable plan/validation readers. This is a latent liveness defect, NOT proof that the blocked public flow is operational.

Original Maestro baseline: 32 tests across 7 files passed. Added diagnostic integration: 5 cases passed their observed-behavior assertions (this means the defect was reproduced, not fixed).

## Actual sequence
1. Present revision V1 in assistant message A; original producer persists its presentation.
2. User asks a question.
3. Re-present identical revision/validation/method in NEW assistant message B with a new tool call ID.
4. Producer returns the original presentation, still bound to A.
5. User immediately replies `aprovo` after B.
6. `recordApproval` returns **HOLD / reply-not-immediate**.

Controls in the same test infrastructure:
- Direct reply to the original presentation → APPROVED.
- New revision/validation presented at B → APPROVED.
- Synthetic approval → HOLD / reply-synthetic.
- Altered presentation output → HOLD / presentation-message-mismatch.

## Cause
Presentation/event identity derives from session, planRevisionID, validationRecordID and methodVersion. Replay equality intentionally ignores assistantMessageID/callID, returning the prior binding. The reply evaluator then requires adjacency to that original message. Retry identity and a newly displayed approval opportunity are conflated.

Sources:
- https://github.com/gmhelmold/HuGR-Orchestra/blob/b0c33d2f6567a2c741240f3c44bc00ca2f01e7e7/packages/opencode/src/maestro/approval-record.ts
- https://github.com/gmhelmold/HuGR-Orchestra/blob/b0c33d2f6567a2c741240f3c44bc00ca2f01e7e7/packages/opencode/src/maestro/approval.ts
- https://github.com/gmhelmold/HuGR-Orchestra/blob/b0c33d2f6567a2c741240f3c44bc00ca2f01e7e7/packages/opencode/src/tool/maestro-approval.ts

## Proposed resolution
Separate immutable plan revision from presentation attempt/idempotency identity. Same-attempt retry must replay; supported redisplay must bind a new visible opportunity and supersede the previous one. Alternatively explicitly refuse unsupported redisplay rather than silently returning an obsolete binding. Do not weaken adjacency or enable the public tool prematurely.

## Completeness criteria
Same-call retry, redisplay after a question, new revision, concurrent attempts, exact payload hashes, old replies, synthetic users and altered output; future public integration when authoritative readers exist.

## Success criteria
Supported approval opportunities accept the direct response to the exact currently displayed revision. Retries do not multiply presentations/decisions and old responses cannot authorize new work.

## Quality standards
Use original producer + database + rendered tool evidence + recordApproval; pure evaluator tests alone are insufficient. Keep explicit boundaries around fixture-inserted visible output.

## Definition of done
Internal regression passes the intended redisplay semantics, controls remain fail-closed, original Maestro suite passes, and public end-to-end proof is required before enabling the currently unavailable tool.

## Invariants
Approval binds the exact visible presentation and direct nonsynthetic user; idempotence must not silently invalidate a new approval opportunity; plan/context/policy/validation/task bindings remain intact.

title: [Atlas][P2] Check reports wouldEmit for a closed-slot violation that emit deterministically refuses
body:
## Scope / evidence
SHA `b0c33d2f6567a2c741240f3c44bc00ca2f01e7e7`, branch `maestro/rebuild-fork-dev-clean`. Newly reproduced using original compiled `composeRuntime`, source-derived grounding, real Git/policy/disk store and BLAKE3; no gate/store doubles. Node v22.17.1. Related audit PR #14.

## Reproduction
Create an otherwise valid fact with the original draft planner. Change only its `predicateSlot` to `unknown-audit-slot` and pass this identical payload/revision first to runtime.check, then to the public atlas-emit handler, with no intervening state mutation.

Observed:
- Valid-slot control: check reports wouldEmit=true.
- Unknown-slot fact: **check reports wouldEmit=true; shape, truth, authz and ratify all pass**.
- Emit of that same unknown-slot fact: **refused, closed-slot-violation**.
- Reopened disk projection remains empty (0 rows): the write protection itself works.

## Root cause
`runGateChain` stops after its four named gate buckets. The closed-13-slot check is enforced later by `upsert`, and its refusal is translated by the real emit path. The dry-run never applies that deterministic condition, contradicting its advertised prediction for unchanged state. This is not a race, disk-full error or legitimate unpredictable commit contention.

Sources:
- https://github.com/gmhelmold/HuGR-Orchestra/blob/b0c33d2f6567a2c741240f3c44bc00ca2f01e7e7/foundation/atlas/packages/adapter-io/src/governed-emit-gates.ts
- https://github.com/gmhelmold/HuGR-Orchestra/blob/b0c33d2f6567a2c741240f3c44bc00ca2f01e7e7/foundation/atlas/packages/knowledge/src/write/upsert.ts
- https://github.com/gmhelmold/HuGR-Orchestra/blob/b0c33d2f6567a2c741240f3c44bc00ca2f01e7e7/foundation/atlas/packages/adapter-io/src/compose-runtime.ts

## Completeness criteria
Audit all deterministic post-ratification refusals, not only this slot case. Cover valid/invalid/absent legacy slots, incumbent constraints, unreadable stores and the declared limits of dry-run prediction separately from transient commit failures.

## Success criteria
An unchanged payload/state cannot receive wouldEmit=true when a known deterministic validation rule will reject it. The same closed-slot reason is discoverable before attempting a write; valid controls still succeed.

## Quality standards
Compare original check and emit using the same runtime and bytes, assert no intervening mutation and no persistence on rejection. Do not weaken the write validator or redefine wouldEmit silently to excuse the mismatch.

## Definition of done
Regression demonstrates the mismatch before the fix and consistent refusal after; authoring/check/emit/closed-slot suites pass; any narrowed prediction semantics are explicit in API/docs.

## Invariants
A dry-run shares deterministic admission semantics with the write; no new slot/address bypass; check remains read-only; no weakening of governance or hidden writes to make prediction accurate.

title: [Own][P2] Final ownership payload is not bounded by its reported selection budget
body:
## Scope / evidence
SHA `b0c33d2f6567a2c741240f3c44bc00ca2f01e7e7`, `maestro/rebuild-fork-dev-clean`; OWN-005 in audit PR #14.

Original `initAst`, source index, `composeRuntime().own`, Git fixture and kernel; no fake Own source. A fixture with 350 tracked TypeScript files under `src` produced:
- `pack.tokenEstimate = 127`
- `pack.shape.contents.length = 350`
- `pack.drill.finer.length = 16`
- Serialized pack size = **8,885 UTF-8 bytes**.

Bytes and model tokens are NOT treated as interchangeable. The measured result demonstrates omitted output from the accounting; the absence of any bound on the returned terrain array supplies the structural unbounded-growth argument. This is not an assertion of a measured 8,885-token payload.

## Cause
`createOwn` applies OWN_CAP to selected candidates and selected pointers, but returns other content—particularly every immediate structural child in terrain, plus other metadata/pointer fields—outside that accounting. Static rendering then adds its receipt and Markdown. A cap on candidate selection is not a cap on the final injected artifact.

Sources:
- https://github.com/gmhelmold/HuGR-Orchestra/blob/b0c33d2f6567a2c741240f3c44bc00ca2f01e7e7/foundation/atlas/packages/retrieval/src/own.ts
- https://github.com/gmhelmold/HuGR-Orchestra/blob/b0c33d2f6567a2c741240f3c44bc00ca2f01e7e7/foundation/atlas/packages/adapter-io/src/own-source.ts
- https://github.com/gmhelmold/HuGR-Orchestra/blob/b0c33d2f6567a2c741240f3c44bc00ca2f01e7e7/foundation/atlas/packages/retrieval/src/own-artifact.ts

## Impact and intended decision
Consumers cannot use the reported estimate/selection cap as a guarantee about total context size. Define whether the budget is candidate-only or final-output; if the latter is promised, account for all serialized sections and provide bounded continuation rather than an unbounded list of pointers replacing an unbounded list of facts.

## Completeness criteria
Account for role, terrain, governing/advisory facts, gotchas, edges, drill, manifest, omitted-fact pointers, receipt and serialization overhead. Define the measurement unit and treatment of mandatory facts/overflow.

## Success criteria
The reported measurement covers the exact delivered representation under its declared unit; increasing terrain or metadata cannot grow output without an explicit bound/continuation/overflow result. Required evidence is never silently truncated.

## Quality standards
Use real large-tree fixtures and adversarial long identifiers. Measure final serialization separately from candidate costs. Never use bytes as exact token counts; tokenizer-specific guarantees must state the tokenizer.

## Definition of done
An end-to-end output-budget regression and valid small-tree controls pass; actual estimator scope is documented, and Own/static renderer consumers agree about boundedness.

## Invariants
Selection budget is not silently advertised as total payload budget; mandatory context is preserved or explicitly held; continuation itself stays bounded; output remains deterministic.

title: [Own][P2] Define and carry graph-coverage authority instead of materializing literal COMPLETE
body:
## Scope and classification
SHA `b0c33d2f6567a2c741240f3c44bc00ca2f01e7e7`, `maestro/rebuild-fork-dev-clean`; OWN-004 in audit PR #14.

**Contract/authority gap, not a reproduced false graph result.** Source inspection proves the missing carrier and constant assignment. Existing valid and adversarial snapshot executions demonstrate byte/blob verification, not that any current committed graph is incomplete.

## Observation
`OwnSnapshot` / `OwnSnapshotUnit` do not carry a graph-coverage verdict or its deriving evidence. `materializeStaticOwnSnapshot()` assigns `graphCoverage: 'COMPLETE'` to every emitted unit. `verifyStaticOwnSnapshot()` verifies the received unit set's materialization and declared source blobs; it does not independently derive the repository's complete graph/unit universe.

The proposed Own protocol says UNDER_APPROX, unavailable graph input and incomplete reverse closure must HOLD. The current snapshot transport cannot represent those conditions for the materializer. A manually reviewed oracle may legitimately be trusted, but the scope and authority of that trust must be explicit rather than inferred from a constant COMPLETE output.

Sources:
- https://github.com/gmhelmold/HuGR-Orchestra/blob/b0c33d2f6567a2c741240f3c44bc00ca2f01e7e7/foundation/atlas/packages/retrieval/src/own-snapshot.ts
- https://github.com/gmhelmold/HuGR-Orchestra/blob/b0c33d2f6567a2c741240f3c44bc00ca2f01e7e7/specs/hugr-maestro/own-protocol.md

## Required decision
Distinguish completeness of static projection relative to an accepted snapshot from completeness of the underlying ownership/dependency graph. Carry the actual graph authority/verdict and its revision, or name the narrower guarantee honestly. Do not infer whole-repository completeness from a nonempty reviewed subset.

## Completeness criteria
Specify unit universe, graph snapshot/revision, unknown-edge handling, review authority, source-anchor coverage and artifact projection coverage separately. Cover the post-Genesis producer and future maintenance verifier, not only the renderer.

## Success criteria
COMPLETE has a documented, inspectable authority and scope; under-approximate/unavailable inputs cannot be silently upgraded by serialization. A valid reviewed snapshot still has a usable path under its explicitly stated trust model.

## Quality standards
Use graph-derived fixtures with both complete and incomplete information; retain byte/blob controls. Do not fabricate absent graph evidence, and do not mislabel this design gap as proof of currently false knowledge.

## Definition of done
Contract and implementation agree, coverage states round-trip, refusal cases are tested, producer/consumer responsibilities are explicit, and static integrity tests continue to pass.

## Invariants
Projection integrity is not graph completeness; freshness of listed sources is not proof all relevant sources were listed; unknown coverage never becomes COMPLETE merely through materialization.

title: [Atlas][P2] Reconcile constant contested=false with the declared incumbent-conflict policy
body:
## Scope and classification
SHA `b0c33d2f6567a2c741240f3c44bc00ca2f01e7e7`, branch `maestro/rebuild-fork-dev-clean`; ATL-003 in audit PR #14.

**Policy/wiring inconsistency requiring an explicit decision. Not a demonstrated cross-scope or T0 privilege bypass.** Original function execution and real handler observations are included, but different text is not automatically a semantic contradiction.

## Confirmed observations
`governed-emit.ts` resolves the real incumbent in each atomic commit attempt, but calls `deriveFastPathVerdicts(truthVerdict.pass, false)`. `runGateChain` likewise supplies literal false. The called function merely returns that flag. Adjacent contracts say contested is derived from a conflicting incumbent, described there as different bytes at the target anchor/slot, and expressly disallow a constant that leaves the gate open.

Original-runtime experiment: emit T2 advisory A; submit B with the same source/anchor/slot/tier but different claim/content hash. Check reports wouldEmit and emit accepts with no token, retaining the two claims. Independently calling the original route with the same valid candidate and contested=true yields full-ratify. Existing same-tier union tests intentionally allow combining claims; this is counterevidence against blindly declaring every update forbidden.

## Required resolution
Define what counts as contested and which authority derives it. If complementary claims should union normally, distinguish them from genuine veto/conflict rather than equating every changed contentHash with contradiction. Then wire that decision into both check and emit, or revise the overstated contract to its actual narrower guarantee. Do not fix this by inventing contested=true for every write or weakening incumbent scope/tier protections.

Sources:
- https://github.com/gmhelmold/HuGR-Orchestra/blob/b0c33d2f6567a2c741240f3c44bc00ca2f01e7e7/foundation/atlas/packages/adapter-io/src/governed-emit.ts
- https://github.com/gmhelmold/HuGR-Orchestra/blob/b0c33d2f6567a2c741240f3c44bc00ca2f01e7e7/foundation/atlas/packages/adapter-io/src/governed-emit-gates.ts
- https://github.com/gmhelmold/HuGR-Orchestra/blob/b0c33d2f6567a2c741240f3c44bc00ca2f01e7e7/foundation/atlas/packages/knowledge/src/ratify/fastpath.ts

## Completeness criteria
Specify genuine conflict/veto, complementary updates, exact duplicates, CREATE, concurrent incumbent changes and origin distinctions. Trace all callers of fast-path verdict construction.

## Success criteria
A declared contested write cannot enter the unratified fast path; ordinary allowed accumulation and duplicates remain allowed under the explicit policy. Check and emit derive the same decision from the same snapshot.

## Quality standards
Use original real-store routes; include allowed-complement controls and explicit conflict/veto fixtures once the contract supplies their authority. Do not claim NLP contradiction from content inequality alone.

## Definition of done
Policy is resolved, source comments/interfaces match enforcement, every production caller supplies the intended state-derived verdict, and union/ratification/incumbent regressions pass.

## Invariants
Gate selection reflects actual declared authority; no invented conflict evidence; scope/T0 protections remain intact; retry re-evaluates the incumbent; absent implementation must not be described as a derived control.

title: [Own][P2] Materializer exits successfully without doing work when invoked through a symlinked path
body:
## Scope / evidence
SHA `b0c33d2f6567a2c741240f3c44bc00ca2f01e7e7`, `maestro/rebuild-fork-dev-clean`; new finding from audit PR #14 follow-up.

Reproduced on macOS / Node v22.17.1 with the ORIGINAL materializer script and compiled contracts/kernel, a real Git fixture, and a valid reviewed snapshot. No patched product code. This was initially encountered via the platform's /tmp → /private/tmp alias and then separately rechecked with an explicitly created directory symlink.

## Paired reproduction
Create symlink `atlas-alias` pointing at the actual Atlas checkout. In the same valid fixture cwd, invoke:
```
node <atlas-alias>/scripts/materialize-own-snapshot.mjs <reviewed.json>
```
Supply the normal implementation override pointing to the REAL compiled own-snapshot implementation, so an absent fixture dist directory is not the cause.

Observed: exit **0**, empty stdout/stderr, and **OWN-SNAPSHOT.json does not exist**.

Invoke the identical command using the canonical real checkout path instead of the symlink alias. Observed: exit 0, explicit wrote message, snapshot and both expected output files exist. Input snapshot, cwd, implementation and dependencies are unchanged.

## Cause
The script's entrypoint check is:
```
resolve(process.argv[1]) === fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)
```
`resolve` normalizes syntax but does not resolve filesystem symlinks. Node resolves the module's real path, so the check fails and `main()` is never called; merely loading the declarations ends successfully.

Source:
https://github.com/gmhelmold/HuGR-Orchestra/blob/b0c33d2f6567a2c741240f3c44bc00ca2f01e7e7/foundation/atlas/scripts/materialize-own-snapshot.mjs

## Completeness criteria
Cover direct real path, relative invocation, symlinked directory, symlinked entrypoint and imported-module use; preserve import safety and existing materializer validation/rollback behavior.

## Success criteria
Supported direct CLI invocation runs main exactly once regardless of path alias, or explicitly refuses with nonzero status. Importing the module still does not run main. Exit 0 cannot silently mean no invocation occurred.

## Quality standards
Use original filesystem symlinks and a valid Git snapshot; assert file existence/content rather than exit code alone. Pair canonical and aliased invocations under identical inputs.

## Definition of done
Current silent no-op reproduction becomes real successful materialization (or documented explicit refusal), import tests remain safe, and original materializer/guard tests pass.

## Invariants
Successful CLI completion corresponds to executed work; alias normalization does not weaken source path safety; module imports do not cause side effects; no partial artifact installation on refusal.
